Maya (Support): Hey @here — ACME reported a burst today around 08:10 UTC where ~40% of requests from eu-west started getting 429s. They expect cross-region failover to route to us-west but they saw all failures coming from eu-west only. They also noticed quota on their dashboard dropped to 0 briefly. Can SRE/Runtime take a look?

Jon (SRE): Copy — can you paste a few request IDs or sample x-request-id from the 429 responses? Need to check whether failures are per-region throttle or global quota enforcement.

Maya (Support): Sample x-request-ids: `req_eu_01a2`, `req_eu_01a3`, `req_eu_01b8`. Customer says response headers looked like: `Retry-After: 3`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-RateLimit-Limit: 120` and a body saying "quota exhausted". They also included the header `X-RW-Region: eu-west-1`.

Priya (Eng Runtime): Thanks. Two likely paths: 1) per-region capacity token bucket hit (we don't auto-burst to another region unless fallback policy allows), or 2) global quota (billing/entitlement) briefly marked as exhausted and the control plane failed to trigger regional fallback. Do we have traces for those request ids?

Jon (SRE): I pulled logs for `req_eu_01a2` — looked like this in the edge logs:```
[2026-07-22T08:10:12Z] req_eu_01a2 - route=eu-west-1 - decision=reject - reason=region_quota_exhausted - tokens=0 - user=acme-corp
[2026-07-22T08:10:13Z] req_eu_01a3 - route=eu-west-1 - decision=reject - reason=burst_protection - tokens=0 - user=acme-corp
```
So the edge rejected before routing to backend. That suggests per-region limiter kicked in.

Maya (Support): ACME claims they have a reserved capacity contract but they were on hosted plan with per-minute burst allowance. Could reserved vs hosted mismatch cause this?

Priya (Eng Runtime): Yes — hosted tenants have dynamic quotas enforced per region, and reserved customers (Dedicated) have dedicated pools. If ACME's account was mis-tagged as hosted after a billing change, the edge would apply hosted per-region burst limits. Sasha, did billing change for ACME today?

Sasha (Product): I just checked — ACME upgraded to Dedicated capacity yesterday but onboarding didn't complete (missing org-tagging in the control plane). Billing shows committed monthly but control plane didn't flip the account flag. That would leave them still subject to hosted per-region caps.

Jon (SRE): That explains the "quota exhausted" header. The cross-region failover behavior: fallbacks only happen when the route decision reaches the control plane that knows to reroute, but our edge rejects early on regional token-bucket breach. If the request is rejected at edge, we don't attempt fallback. We probably need a short-circuit where edge returns a 202-like deferred or proxies to fallback when org has dedicated capacity but control plane stale.

Maya (Support): For immediate customer mitigation, what's the recommended workaround we can tell them?

Priya (Eng Runtime): Two practical options: 1) Temporarily increase hosted burst quota for acme-corp (hotfix from control plane) or 2) re-tag them in control plane as dedicated so edge uses dedicated pool routing. For quick action do (1) — I can patch their hosted quota to add +200 tokens for 10 minutes.

Jon (SRE): I'll also add a short-term edge rule to allow fallback proxying for requests that have header `X-Org-Override: dedicated` for debugging (we'll require telemetry and only enable for 5 mins). Use with care.

Maya (Support): I'll send both options to ACME. Also they asked for repro steps so they can validate after we patch. Can we provide a curl they can run to exercise fallback?

Priya (Eng Runtime): Provide them this repro curl (will show 429 if edge rejects):```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -H "X-RW-Region: eu-west-1" \\n  -d '{"model":"rw-large","input":"test burst"}'
```
If they get 429 with `Retry-After` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` that's region limiter. After we flip tag or increase tokens, rerun with `-H "X-RW-Region: us-west-2"` — if request succeeds, then cross-region failover works but edge prevented it initially.

rate-limiter-bot: Notice: quota-adjustment applied to acme-corp: +200 tokens (temporary, expires in 10m). Trace: https://internal.redwood/trace/trace-9ab3

Jon (SRE): Applied the short edge proxy rule now (test window 5m). Tags show `acme-corp` now has control-plane flag pending.

Maya (Support): ACME just confirmed they're green after your patch. They ran the curl twice: once in eu-west got a 200 after token bump, once in us-west worked earlier. :tada: They asked if we can prevent this class of incident.

Priya (Eng Runtime): Longer term we should change edge logic: when region limiter rejects and customer has dedicated capacity in control plane (even if pending), the edge should attempt an immediate fallback to the customer's preferred alternate region rather than outright reject. Also add metric alert when region limiter rejects for orgs with active committed capacity.

Sasha (Product): Filed feature request: "edge-fallback-for-committed-orgs" and assigned to eng-runtime. Estimate: 2 sprints for design + test harness. Also we'll add an onboarding check so control plane tagging can't be left pending after billing commit.

Maya (Support): Great — I'll mark the ticket as resolved with ACME and include the repro + what we changed. Thanks all.

Jon (SRE): Follow-up ops note: collect a sample of edge rejects for last 24h and correlate with billing state; I can run a query and share results.

Priya (Eng Runtime): Added a small rollout: edge will now include `X-Fallback-Attempt: true` header when we attempt proxying during the debug window. We'll remove after incident window.

Maya (Support): Closing here — ping me if anyone needs logs attached for the customer case.
